title: LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B BF16 vs groxaxo GPTQ-Pro INT4 g64, same RTX 3090
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 24GiB; same physical GPU0 for both precision configurations
hardware_context: Ubuntu x86_64, Intel Core i7-12700KF, CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.10.0, Transformers 5.21.0
test_dataset: Google FLEURS en_us and es_419 test split, first 50 utterances per language, human read-speech
audio_preprocessing: Per-file simulated 8-kHz, G.711 mu-law-equivalent companding followed by 16-kHz input resampling; not live PSTN
calibration: 16 separate synthetic LFM3-generated English/Spanish call phrases, not benchmark speech
quant_method: GPTQ-Pro quality_4bit W4 G64, 142 selectively quantized language-backbone projections; audio components preserved BF16
important_methodology_limits: WER is a small-sample heldout measurement, not a statistically proven ranking.
Results include one pass per precision; no repeated-run latency variability evaluation.
Latency is model generation after preprocessing; not real-time SIP/PSTN end-to-end latency.
FLEURS human read speech lacks New Zealand telephone-call noise and conversational disfluency.
PyTorch allocated tensor memory is not total nvidia-smi process VRAM or evidence of concurrency capacity.
Speech quality, Spanish instruction adherence, booking correctness, VAD/barge-in, concurrency and TTFA are not established.
